description:
Here's a description of the line plot, following the guidelines:

The plot illustrates the relationship between the number of missing pieces in an M-Cube and the number of possible solutions. The x-axis is labeled “# Missing pieces” and has a linear scale ranging from 1 to 6, with tick labels at each integer value. The y-axis is labeled “# Possible solutions” and uses a logarithmic scale, ranging from 10<sup>1</sup> to 10<sup>8</sup>, with tick labels at each power of 10.  A line, colored orange and marked with circular data points, represents “Flip needed”; it begins at approximately (1, 10<sup>1</sup>) and increases to approximately (6, 10<sup>8</sup>), showing a steady increase with a slight curvature. A dashed line, colored blue and marked with circular data points, represents “Flip ignored”; it begins at approximately (1, 10<sup>1</sup>) and increases to approximately (6, 10<sup>6</sup>), also showing a steady increase with a slight curvature.  Two points are specifically labeled: “CUBE-easy” at approximately (2, 10<sup>1</sup>) and “CUBE” at approximately (6, 10<sup>8</sup>).
